input.rationale: Record the mechanism the two compaction children share, so a reader of the parent account can see in one entry why both paths inherit the drift: each derives the index it may compact from a value the node computes for itself (trim from the minimum recorded accepted index, the snapshot call from the receiving node's decided index) and neither compares that bound with the entries the log actually holds. The fact cites the derivations and the two receipts that exercised it (trim compacting 7 and the snapshot call compacting 8, both over logs of six indices), which are the same receipts the child accounts rest on.

knowledge.statement: Both compaction paths derive the index they may compact from values the node computes for itself rather than from what any replica holds: trim takes the minimum of the accepted indexes the leader has recorded for the configuration (or refuses an explicit index above that minimum) and the snapshot path takes the decided index of the node that receives the call, while neither bound is compared against the entries the node's own log contains. The consequences follow from that: with the recorded or decided values drifted above the content, trim compacted index 7 and the snapshot path compacted index 8 for logs of six indices.
knowledge.conditions: Capture snapshot; leader role for trim, any role for the snapshot call. Exercised in receipts ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a (trim: recorded values 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content, compacted 7, events 9-15) and e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c (snapshot: decided 9 over six indices of content, a request at 8 accepted, compacted 8, snapshot holding none of the five decided entries, events 0-5), both after the drift the parent question witnesses.

knowledge.statement: InternalStorage::sync_log sets accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and, when LogSync.stopsign is Some, adds one further index for that StopSign before returning; it does not subtract the LogSync's prefix, so when sync_idx already addresses the StopSign's own index the replica's accepted index ends up one larger than the entries it holds, and each further re-synchronization of the same replica adds one more index while its content is unchanged. SequencePaxos::create_log_sync does not adjust sync_idx for a StopSign already present on the sender: it uses its caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged and attaches the sender's stored StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Reached when a replica applies an AcceptSync or a leader applies a Promise whose LogSync carries stopsign = Some; the accounting is unconditional with respect to whether the resumed prefix already contained a StopSign. Exercised in six receipts, including three consecutive rounds of two-follower reconnection in receipt 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d, where the two followers went from six indices of content to reported accepted index 7, then 8, then 9 (events 41, 42; 44, 45; 47, 48) while their decided-log read stayed at one element and the leader's decided index followed the same values (events 43, 46, 49).

knowledge.statement: The inflated accepted index follows from the resume point being compared against the index the StopSign occupies in the receiving replica's accounting: sync_log computes accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and adds one for a carried StopSign, while the StopSign occupies the index accepted_idx - 1 and the sender attaches it without shifting sync_idx. knowledge.statement: A leader in the accept phase accepts a decision at the accepted index reported by any matching-ballot Accepted message: it records that index for the sender, and if the index exceeds its own decided index and a write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covers it, it sets its decided index to exactly that reported index, without comparing it against the length of its own log or against its own accepted index.

knowledge.statement: A candidate leader whose own promise metadata is not the maximum among the promises it collects syncs its own log from the promise metadata of another node: handle_majority_promises passes that promise's LogSync to sync_log together with the maximum decided index, so the candidate's own accepted index is recomputed from that LogSync and can exceed the number of indices it holds when the LogSync's resume point already covers a carried StopSign.

knowledge.assertion: the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index

knowledge.statement: When a candidate becomes leader it adopts two independently ordered inputs in one call: the log comes from the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) with pid only as tiebreak, while the decided index is the maximum decided index over all recorded promises; sync_log then writes that decided index and the adopted log in the same storage transaction, and the leader path contains no clamp comparing the two.
knowledge.conditions: Reached in handle_majority_promises after a prepare quorum (leader.rs 257-285) together with set_promise (util.rs 131-149) and get_max_decided_idx (util.rs 168-177); the two orders coincide whenever the promise with the greatest accepted round and index also reports the greatest decided index, which is the case in every observed run of this investigation. Sourced only; no execution has yet produced a disagreement between the two orders.

knowledge.statement: For a candidate that syncs from the greatest promise, the accepted index it ends with is the adopted promise's own accepted count whenever the resume point lies inside that promise's content: sync_idx is the candidate's decided or accepted index, the suffix is the adopted promise's log from there, and the carried StopSign adds the same one index the adopted promise already counted, so the two accounting terms cancel. Whenever the resume point lies beyond that content the suffix is empty and the candidate ends at sync_idx plus the StopSign term. A disagreement between the adopted decided index and the entries held therefore needs some promise reporting a decided index above the adopted promise's content.
knowledge.conditions: Follows from the two branches of the follower's Promise (common_prefix = prep.decided_idx when na > prep.n_accepted, prep.accepted_idx when equal and greater) and sync_log's accepted accounting; the adopted promise is the strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx). Sourced; the three-node runs of this investigation had the greatest promise also reporting the greatest decided index, so the disagreement never arose there.

knowledge.statement: Repeated re-synchronizations of replicas that already hold the StopSign make the cluster's reported accepted and decided indices drift one further index per round while the log content stays fixed: the leader keeps adopting the maximum reported accepted index as its decided index, so the reported decided index follows the drift while the leader's own accepted index does not, leaving its decided index above the entries it holds and its decided-log read unusable.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster after a decided StopSign, each round being a pair of public reconnected() calls and nothing else; observed over three rounds in receipt 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d: followers' accepted and decided 7 then 8 then 9 (events 41, 42, 44, 45, 47, 48) and the leader's decided 7 then 8 then 9 with accepted 6 and is_reconfigured false each round (events 43, 46, 49). No bound on the number of rounds, on the counter values or on any repair inside the sealed configuration was observed; the run stopped after three rounds by construction.

knowledge.statement: Trim's bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes and both trim paths respect it: with no explicit index that minimum is used, and an explicit index above it is refused with that same minimum reported. The bound can therefore exceed only the content of replicas whose recorded accepted index has itself drifted; a replica whose report is still truthful keeps the bound at or below its own content, and no in-cluster promise or log sync can then ask for a prefix below the compacted index.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot path bounds a user-supplied index by the decided index of the node that receives the call, not by any recorded accepted index and not by another node's decided index: an index equal to that decided index is mapped to the decided log without the StopSign, a lower index is used as given, and a greater index is refused with the decided index reported; the snapshot itself is then created from the storage range that starts at the current compacted index.

knowledge.statement: On a leader whose decided index has drifted above its content, the snapshot path accepts a user-supplied index inside that drifted decided index, advances the compacted index to it, and builds the snapshot from a storage range that starts at the previous compacted index; when that range lies past the entries the log holds, the storage returns nothing and the snapshot is created from an empty slice, so the entries are no longer reachable through the log and the snapshot that now represents the region holds none of them.

result.summary: Recorded the mechanism the two compaction children share, so a reader of the parent account can see in one entry why both paths inherit the drift: each derives the index it may compact from a value the node computes for itself — trim from the minimum of the accepted indexes the leader has recorded for the configuration (and it refuses an explicit index above that minimum), the snapshot call from the decided index of the node that receives the call — and neither bound is compared against the entries the node's own log contains. The fact cites the derivations as sources and the two receipts that exercised it: trim compacted index 7 and the snapshot call compacted index 8, both over logs of six indices of content, after the drift the parent question witnesses (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15 and e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). This complements the two stale-condition corrections from the previous turns, so both compaction behaviours now show their executed basis, and it gives the final report a single citable statement of the shared cause rather than two separate ones. No execution was requested this turn; incomplete are the parent drift's bound/repair probe after many more rounds and leader changes, the trim child's storage-side route probe, the snapshot child's peer and follower sampling, timers and loss triggers, larger clusters, persistence, and any further independent lead.

knowledge.statement: When a candidate becomes leader it adopts two independently ordered inputs in one call: the log comes from the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) with pid only as tiebreak, while the decided index is the maximum decided index over all recorded promises; sync_log then writes that decided index and the adopted log in the same storage transaction, and the leader path contains no clamp comparing the two.
knowledge.conditions: Reached in handle_majority_promises after a prepare quorum (leader.rs 257-285) together with set_promise (util.rs 131-149) and get_max_decided_idx (util.rs 168-177); the two orders coincide whenever the promise with the greatest accepted round and index also reports the greatest decided index, which is the case in every observed run of this investigation. Sourced only; no execution has yet produced a disagreement between the two orders.

knowledge.statement: For a candidate that syncs from the greatest promise, the accepted index it ends with is the adopted promise's own accepted count whenever the resume point lies inside that promise's content: sync_idx is the candidate's decided or accepted index, the suffix is the adopted promise's log from there, and the carried StopSign adds the same one index the adopted promise already counted, so the two accounting terms cancel. Whenever the resume point lies beyond that content the suffix is empty and the candidate ends at sync_idx plus the StopSign term. A disagreement between the adopted decided index and the entries held therefore needs some promise reporting a decided index above the adopted promise's content.
knowledge.conditions: Follows from the two branches of the follower's Promise (common_prefix = prep.decided_idx when na > prep.n_accepted, prep.accepted_idx when equal and greater) and sync_log's accepted accounting; the adopted promise is the strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx). Sourced; the three-node runs of this investigation had the greatest promise also reporting the greatest decided index, so the disagreement never arose there.

knowledge.statement: Repeated re-synchronizations of replicas that already hold the StopSign make the cluster's reported accepted and decided indices drift one further index per round while the log content stays fixed: the leader keeps adopting the maximum reported accepted index as its decided index, so the reported decided index follows the drift while the leader's own accepted index does not, leaving its decided index above the entries it holds and its decided-log read unusable.
